Name: layer_ablation_function
Title: Which Layer of Evo2 Encodes Gene Function? A Layer-wise Ablation Study
Experiment: Extract embeddings from four different Evo2-7B layers: an early layer (blocks.4.mlp.l3), two middle layers (blocks.14.mlp.l3, blocks.21.mlp.l3), and the late layer used in the baseline (blocks.28.mlp.l3). Train the same MLP classifier on each set of embeddings with identical hyperparameters and train/test splits. Compare AUROC, accuracy, and F1 across layers. Additionally, compute a one-hot nucleotide baseline (4-mer frequency features from the promoter+CDS sequence) to establish a non-learned lower bound. Plot AUROC vs. layer depth to reveal whether functional information accumulates progressively through the network or emerges at a specific depth.

Name: triclass_functional_prediction
Title: Beyond Binary Classification: Can Evo2 Embeddings Distinguish Three Distinct Functional Gene Classes?
Experiment: Extend the baseline to a 3-class problem by adding metabolic enzyme genes from the glycolysis/gluconeogenesis pathway (KEGG hsa00010) as a third class, alongside DNA repair (label=0) and tumor suppressors (label=1). Assign metabolism genes label=2. Fetch ~40-50 glycolysis genes using the existing KEGG API infrastructure. Modify the MLP classifier to output 3 classes: change final layer to nn.Linear(prev, 3) and use CrossEntropyLoss instead of BCEWithLogitsLoss. Modify evaluation to compute per-class precision, recall, F1, and overall accuracy. Generate and save a 3×3 confusion matrix to analyze misclassification patterns (e.g., are DNA repair genes ever confused with metabolism? Are TSGs closer to DNA repair or metabolism in embedding space?). Compare performance against a random baseline (33% accuracy) and report whether the model achieves significantly above-chance multi-class separation. The key result is whether Evo2 embeddings encode functional distinctions beyond a single binary axis, suggesting compositional functional representation.

Name: region_decomposition_analysis
Title: Decomposing Functional Information: Do Promoters and Coding Sequences Contribute Distinct Signals to Evo2's Gene Function Representations?
Experiment: Modify build_dataset() to store promoter (2kb upstream) and CDS as separate fields. Create three embedding sets by modifying get_evo2_embeddings() to accept a sequence_type parameter: (1) promoter-only, (2) CDS-only, (3) promoter+CDS concatenated (baseline). Extract embeddings from blocks.28.mlp.l3 for each. Train identical MLP classifiers on each embedding set using the same train/test splits and hyperparameters. Evaluate and compare AUROC, accuracy, and F1 for each condition. Compute mean sequence lengths for promoter vs. CDS to document the length difference. Calculate a complementarity score: AUROC(promoter+CDS) - max(AUROC(promoter), AUROC(CDS)) to quantify synergistic information gain from combining regions. Analyze per-class performance: report separate F1 scores for DNA repair and TSG classes under each condition to test whether CDS is more informative for DNA repair genes (protein domain hypothesis) while promoters are more informative for TSGs (regulatory co-expression hypothesis). Output a results table with columns: [sequence_type, mean_length, overall_AUROC, DNA_repair_F1, TSG_F1].

Name: unsupervised_embedding_geometry
Title: Unsupervised Functional Structure in Evo2 Embeddings: Do Gene Functions Emerge as Natural Clusters?
Experiment: Test whether Evo2 embeddings naturally separate functional classes without supervision. After extracting embeddings from blocks.28.mlp.l3 (reuse cached embeddings), add a new function analyze_embedding_geometry() that: (1) Applies k-means clustering (k=2, n_init=50, random_state=seed) on the full embedding space and computes Adjusted Rand Index (ARI) against true labels to measure unsupervised accuracy. (2) Computes silhouette score using true functional labels to quantify cluster separation quality. (3) Performs a permutation test: shuffle labels 1000 times, recompute silhouette scores, and calculate p-value as the fraction of permuted scores >= observed score to test statistical significance. (4) Creates a random embedding baseline: generate random Gaussian embeddings with same shape, compute ARI and silhouette, showing Evo2 structure is non-trivial. (5) Projects embeddings to 2D using PCA (top 2 components) and UMAP (n_neighbors=15, min_dist=0.1), creating a 1x2 subplot figure with points colored by true labels (DNA repair=blue, TSG=red), saved as embedding_geometry.png. (6) Reports explained variance of top 2 PCs. Call this function after embedding extraction in run() and save metrics to unsupervised_metrics.json including: ARI, silhouette_score, silhouette_pvalue, random_ARI, random_silhouette, pca_explained_var. Compare ARI to supervised test accuracy to quantify the gap. Key result: if ARI > 0.3 and p < 0.05, embeddings encode statistically significant unsupervised functional structure.

Name: handcrafted_feature_baseline
Title: Do Evo2 Embeddings Outperform Handcrafted Sequence Features? Validating Deep Representations Against Interpretable Biological Baselines
Experiment: Add a new function compute_sequence_features(seq, promoter_len=2000) that extracts: (1) GC content for promoter and CDS regions separately (2 features), (2) sequence lengths for promoter, CDS, and total (3 features), (3) CpG observed/expected ratio for promoter region calculated as: cpg_count / (c_count * g_count / promoter_len) (1 feature), (4) normalized 3-mer frequency vector (64 features). Apply PCA (n_components=20, random_state=0) to the 3-mer frequencies to reduce dimensionality and prevent overfitting on the small dataset. Concatenate all features into a vector of ~26 dimensions. In run(), after loading the dataset, compute handcrafted features for all genes. Train three separate MLP classifiers (same architecture/hyperparameters) on: (A) Evo2 embeddings only (baseline), (B) handcrafted features only, (C) concatenated Evo2 + handcrafted features. Use identical train/test splits for all three. Evaluate and save results to feature_comparison.json containing AUROC, accuracy, and F1 for each condition across all seeds. Compute delta_auroc = mean(evo2_auroc) - mean(handcrafted_auroc) and perform a paired t-test across seeds to test significance. Compute complementarity_gain = mean(combined_auroc) - max(mean(evo2_auroc), mean(handcrafted_auroc)) to quantify whether features provide orthogonal information. As a secondary analysis, fit sklearn LogisticRegression (C=1.0, max_iter=1000) on handcrafted features and save the top 10 features by absolute coefficient value to feature_importance.json for biological interpretation. Key hypothesis: if delta_auroc > 0.10 with p < 0.05, Evo2 captures functional information beyond simple sequence statistics.

Name: zero_shot_functional_transfer
Title: Zero-Shot Functional Transfer: Can Evo2 Embeddings Generalize to Unseen Gene Function Categories?
Experiment: Test whether functional classifiers trained on one gene pair transfer to completely different, held-out functional categories. Define two gene pairs: (A) DNA repair vs tumor suppressors [reuse existing cached data], (B) metabolic enzymes (glycolysis KEGG hsa00010) vs signaling proteins (MAPK pathway KEGG hsa04010). Modify build_dataset() to accept a dataset_name parameter ('repair_vs_tsg' or 'metabolic_vs_signaling') and fetch ~40-50 genes per class for pair B using the existing KEGG infrastructure. Extract embeddings from blocks.28.mlp.l3 for both pairs (cache separately). Implement bidirectional zero-shot transfer with random baseline: (1) Train MLP classifier on pair A using 80/20 train/test split (seed=0), evaluate on pair A test set (within_domain_accuracy) and on the complete pair B dataset which was never seen during training (zero_shot_accuracy). (2) Symmetrically, train on pair B, test on pair B test set and complete pair A dataset. (3) For each transfer direction, create a random label baseline: shuffle the target pair labels 100 times, compute zero-shot accuracy each time, report mean and std as zero_shot_random_mean and zero_shot_random_std. Use identical model architecture and hyperparameters (same as baseline experiment) for both directions. Additionally, compute embedding geometry on full datasets (all genes, no train/test split): for each pair, calculate mean intra-class cosine similarity (average pairwise similarity within each functional class, then average across classes) and mean inter-class cosine similarity. Define cohesion_score = intra_class_similarity - inter_class_similarity. Save results to zero_shot_transfer.json with: {pair_A_to_B: {within_acc, zero_shot_acc, zero_shot_random_mean, zero_shot_random_std}, pair_B_to_A: {within_acc, zero_shot_acc, zero_shot_random_mean, zero_shot_random_std}, geometry: {pair_A: {intra_sim, inter_sim, cohesion}, pair_B: {intra_sim, inter_sim, cohesion}}}. Key hypothesis: if zero_shot_acc > zero_shot_random_mean + 2*std (p<0.05 by normal approximation) and mean zero_shot_acc across both directions > 60%, Evo2 embeddings encode transferable functional representations.
